title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1986 'Analysis situs' draft (cote 156-4). In it Grothendieck builds an axiomatic, combinatorial framework for 'figures'. A figure F is a stratified space: a support |F| together with a finite set Σ_F of open strata satisfying a frontier-type condition. An elementary figure is the closure of one open stratum X with its induced strata, written F_X. The set of all elementary figures is F_el. A general figure can be encoded as a subset of F_el, one element F_X for each stratum X. F_el already carries an order ≤: inclusion of elementary figures, the face relation. On p.13 he defined a subdivision F' of F by two conditions: |F'| = |F|, and the equivalence relation on |F| given by F' is finer than the one given by F. He also noted that subdivisions of elementary figures need not be elementary.

Page 14 restates this through a second order relation, refinement, written F' ≪ F. F' refines F if every open stratum of F' is contained in an open stratum of F, which is necessarily unique since strata are disjoint. Consequences: (i) |F'| ⊂ |F|, but not necessarily |F'| = |F|. (ii) Inclusion of figures (every open stratum of F' is an open stratum of F) implies refinement, so ≪ is a weaker and more permissive relation than ⊂. Grothendieck calls it 'plus fine/plus forte'. (iii) Refinement of arbitrary figures reduces to the order ≪ on F_el: F' ≪ F iff for every stratum X' of F' there is a stratum X of F with F'_{X'} ≪ F_X.

Proof of (iii): Suppose X' ⊂ X. Then the closure of X' lies in the closure of X. Every stratum of F' in that closure lies in some stratum of F. By the frontier condition that stratum lies in the closure of X, so F'_{X'} ≪ F_X. Conversely, X' is an open stratum of F'_{X'}, so it lies in some stratum of F_X, which is a stratum of F.

Page 15 then completes the picture. F_el carries two structures, ≤ and ≪. For elementary figures, x ≤ x' iff x and x' are compatible and x ≪ x'. A subdivision is a refinement with the same support, equivalently a refinement that is maximal for ⊂ among the refinements of F. The aim is a purely order-theoretic or combinatorial axiomatization of stratified 'tame' spaces and their subdivisions: a poset-with-extra-structure model of PL/tame topology, in the spirit of the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse.
errors: Terminology: Grothendieck calls the refinement relation 'plus fine que l'inclusion' and 'plus forte que celle d'inclusion'. As sets of pairs, inclusion implies refinement, so ≪ contains more pairs and is the weaker (coarser) relation. The intended meaning (refinement generalizes inclusion) is clear, but the wording is inverted relative to standard usage.

Uniqueness of the containing stratum ('unique, bien sûr') and the reduction to F_el silently use the frontier condition, i.e. closure of a stratum is a union of strata. That condition is presumably part of the definition of figure on earlier pages, but it is not restated here.

ideas.what: Refinement order on stratified figures: every open stratum of F' lies in an open stratum of F, implying |F'| ⊂ |F|
ideas.modern_name: refinement of stratifications / of cell decompositions (partial, not necessarily same support)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Whitney–Thom stratification theory; combinatorial topology; o-minimal cell decomposition, van den Dries)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tame topology and stratifications in general terms, not this formal definition

ideas.what: Reduction of refinement of arbitrary figures to a refinement order on the set F_el of elementary (closed-cell) figures
ideas.modern_name: local criterion for refinement via closed strata / face poset encoding

ideas.what: Encoding figures as subsets of F_el equipped with two order relations (≤ face/inclusion, ≪ refinement), with subdivision = refinement maximal for ⊂ (equivalently, same support)
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic/combinatorial model of tame (PL/o-minimal) stratified spaces; posets of cells
ideas.usually_credited_to: related ideas: o-minimal structures (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight); Shiota's work on tame topology

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an order-theoretic axiomatization of 'figures' (stratified tame spaces). A single set F_el of elementary figures carries a face order ≤ and a refinement order ≪, with ≤ = compatibility + ≪, and subdivisions are maximal refinements. This is an unpublished attempt to make the Esquisse's 'topologie modérée' axiomatic. The page itself is foundational bookkeeping rather than a result.
missed.quote: C'est une relation d'ordre sur l'ens des figures, plus forte que celle d'inclusion ... car F' raffine F ssi pour tout (X' ∈ Σ'_{F'}), ∃ X ∈ Σ'_F, telle que F'_{X'} raffine F_X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents the concrete shape of Grothendieck's tame-topology programme, otherwise known only from the Esquisse. It could be compared with o-minimal and definable-stratification frameworks, and with exit-path/poset models of stratified spaces (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka). It is of historical interest; it is not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The definitions and the reduction lemma are routine and correct. The interest is mainly historical: concrete evidence of Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at a combinatorial axiomatization of tame stratified spaces, which is not published.
